description: Shared BOUNDARY CONTRACT CORPUS for sync write-back ops (docs/architecture/sync.md §9, ADR-0025, D-12, FR-OF-2, NFR-TST-1, #585). Concrete ops run through BOTH the owning service's real validate*Op (Go) and the client's real validateSyncOps (Dart), asserting identical accept/reject decisions and identical (field, code, message) outcomes. One artifact, two consumers — see contracts/validation/README.md.

conventions.op: A sync op exactly as it goes on the wire. Field paths in expect/serverOnly are OP-RELATIVE: the server prefixes them with ops[i]. — the harness strips that prefix, which is itself part of what is checked.
conventions.expect: The field errors BOTH sides must report for this op — same field path, same code, same message — and nothing else. An empty list means both sides must ACCEPT the op.
conventions.serverOnly: Field errors ONLY the authoritative server reports, because the rule is in the description's serverOnly list (ownership lookups, extensible vocabularies, the per-activity-type attribute schema, breakdown, patch-changes-any) or because the client structurally cannot run it. The client must report NONE of these. `message` is optional here — a server-only message is not mirrored in the description, so pinning it would only make the corpus break when an unrelated vocabulary grows.
conventions.@repeat: A string of the exact form "@repeat:<count>:<unit>" expands to <unit> repeated <count> times, on both sides, so a 10001-character notes field does not have to be spelled out. Nothing else in a string is interpreted.
conventions.escaping: Avoid < > and & in string values: Go's encoding/json escapes them by default and Dart's jsonEncode does not, which would make the two sides measure different byte lengths for the maxBytes rule.
conventions.entityType: Routes the case to the owning service's validator. It is NOT read from op.entity_type, so a case can deliberately carry a wrong entity_type and still reach the right validator.

ids.note: The Go harness pre-resolves ownership for the apiary/journey/assignee ids above and for nothing else, so `unowned` is what a cross-organization reference looks like. Ownership is server-only by design (the device cannot decide it offline).
ids.whyRepeatedDigits: Each id is a single repeated digit ON PURPOSE and must stay that way. gitleaks' generic-api-key rule fires on a high-entropy value next to a keyword, and `api` is one of its keywords — so a realistic-looking UUID under `apiary_id` reads as a credential and fails `task repo:secrets` on every such line. These are opaque wire values that the cases only need to be well-formed and distinct, so low entropy costs the corpus nothing, and keeping it means the secret scanner stays unweakened for this file instead of being allowlisted past it.

cases.name: apiary/patch/partial-is-not-a-full-row
cases.why: #378: a patch carries only the columns that changed. Demanding name or location of one would reject a valid edit with no server to overrule it.

cases.name: apiary/delete/carries-no-payload
cases.why: Both validators return right after the envelope checks on a delete, so no data-shaped rule may fire against an op that has no data.

cases.name: apiary/delete/ignores-a-payload-that-would-otherwise-fail
cases.why: Pins the delete short-circuit itself: this data would produce three errors on a put.

cases.name: apiary/put/name-empty-string-counts-as-absent
cases.why: absentWhen: empty — validateApiaryOp guards `*data.Name == ""`, not TrimSpace.

cases.name: apiary/put/name-whitespace-only-is-accepted
cases.why: The other half of absentWhen: empty. Describing name as `blank` would make the client reject a name this service accepts.

expect.message: name must be at most 200 characters

cases.name: apiary/put/name-length-is-utf8-bytes-not-code-units
cases.why: 101 accented characters are 202 UTF-8 bytes but only 101 Dart string units. Go compares len() on a UTF-8 string, so measuring anything else on the client rejects Portuguese names this service accepts.

expect.message: name must be at most 200 characters

cases.name: apiary/patch/name-too-long
cases.why: A cap applies to a patch as well as a put — only `required` is op-gated.

expect.message: name must be at most 200 characters
notes must be at most 10000 characters
place_label must be at most 200 characters
dgav_registration_number must be at most 50 characters

cases.name: apiary/put/location-missing-entirely
cases.why: entityChecks.requiredGroup — reported under the synthetic path data.location, which is neither coordinate's own path.

cases.name: apiary/patch/longitude-without-latitude
cases.why: entityChecks.requiredWhenPresent — the failure is reported against the MISSING half, not against the field that triggered the rule.

expect.message: location_lat is required when location_lon is set
location_lon is required when location_lat is set

cases.name: apiary/put/several-rules-fail-at-once
cases.why: Aggregation: a validator that returned on the first failure would drop two of these.

expect.message: notes must be at most 10000 characters
op must be put, patch or delete

cases.name: apiary/put/entity-type-not-a-known-type
cases.why: entityTypeCheck is descriptive-only for the client, which dispatches BY entity_type and so passes an unknown one through to the server. Pinning the message here is what keeps the described string honest.

serverOnly.message: entity_type must be apiary, apiary_counter or stock_declaration
serverOnly.why: The client never reaches an entity type it has no rules for.

serverOnly.message: patch must change at least one field
serverOnly.why: serverOnly: defined over an exact field list, so a field added server-side would turn valid patches into client-side rejections.

cases.name: apiary_counter/patch/without-a-value
cases.why: #378: a value-less patch is an idempotent no-op here, not a rejection.

cases.name: apiary_counter/patch/apiary-id-missing
cases.why: The identity pair is required on BOTH op kinds — a counter is identified by (apiary_id, counter_type), never by the client row id.

serverOnly.why: serverOnly (D-20): the vocabulary is extensible server-side, and a frozen client copy would reject a newer value permanently.

expect.message: op must be put or patch for apiary_counter (counters have no delete)

cases.name: apiary_counter/delete/without-data
cases.why: validateCounterOp has no delete short-circuit (delete is not an allowed kind for it at all), while the client's evaluator short-circuits every delete. The client therefore under-reports here, which is the safe direction — it defers to the server — but it is an asymmetry, so it is recorded rather than left to be discovered.

expect.message: op must be put or patch for apiary_counter (counters have no delete)

serverOnly.why: Reached only because validateCounterOp keeps validating an op kind it has already rejected.

cases.name: stock_declaration/delete/valid
cases.why: Unlike a counter, a declaration is an independent record and DOES accept delete.

expect.message: declared_on must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form

cases.name: stock_declaration/patch/declared-on-is-a-date-that-does-not-exist
cases.why: Go's time.Parse range-checks the day; Dart's DateTime.parse silently rolls 2026-02-30 into March, so only a calendar round-trip on the client keeps the two sides equal.

expect.message: declared_on must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form
dgav_registration_number must be at most 50 characters

cases.name: stock_declaration/patch/notes-too-long
cases.why: A declaration's notes cap is 2000, not apiaries' 10000 — a corpus case per entity is what keeps a copy-pasted cap from going unnoticed.

expect.message: notes must be at most 2000 characters

cases.name: stock_declaration/patch/breakdown-is-not-an-array
cases.why: breakdown is serverOnly and is an ARRAY — describing it as a jsonObject would reject every declaration. The client must stay silent about it; this case is what proves the exclusion is deliberate rather than a divergence.

serverOnly.message: breakdown must be a JSON array
serverOnly.why: serverOnly: a bounded array of client-owned objects, outside the field-check vocabulary.

serverOnly.message: patch must change at least one field
serverOnly.why: serverOnly, for the same reason as apiaries'.

expect.message: op must be put, patch or delete

cases.name: activity/patch/attributes-only
cases.why: #378: neither apiary_id, type nor occurred_at is demanded of a partial update.

serverOnly.why: serverOnly: cross-organization ownership needs server state the device does not have offline.

expect.message: occurred_at must be a YYYY-MM-DD date
attributes must be a JSON object

cases.name: activity/patch/attributes-is-an-explicit-null
cases.why: An explicit null is present-but-not-an-object on both sides, not absent — the server unmarshals it into a nil map and rejects it.

expect.message: attributes must be a JSON object

serverOnly.why: serverOnly (D-20): the activity-type registry is extensible server-side.
serverOnly: the per-activity-type attribute-bag schema is a rich schema, not a mechanical constraint.

expect.message: op must be put, patch or delete

serverOnly.why: The client dispatches BY entity_type and so cannot fail this check.

cases.name: journey/patch/status-only
cases.why: #378's concrete case: closing a journey uploads only the status column.

expect.message: name must be at most 200 characters

serverOnly.why: serverOnly (D-20): status is not described at all, so the client has no rule to run.

expect.message: default_attributes must be a JSON object

cases.name: journey/patch/default-attributes-is-an-explicit-null
cases.why: An explicit null is how a journey's defaults get CLEARED: PowerSync's upload diff emits a column key only when it changed, and a column cleared to SQL NULL is emitted as JSON null (verified against powersync-sqlite-core — contracts/validation/README.md). Both sides accept it and read it as "no defaults"; the description says so with absentWhen: jsonNull. Contrast activity/patch/attributes-is-an-explicit-null, which is still REJECTED — the relaxation is per-field, not a change to what jsonObject means.

cases.name: journey/patch/clearing-defaults-alongside-a-real-edit
cases.why: The op a device actually produces when a user changes a journey's main activity type, which clears the defaults section client-side: one patch carrying the changed column AND the cleared bag. This is the edit that was dead-lettered before the fix.

cases.name: journey/patch/default-attributes-over-the-byte-cap
cases.why: maxBytes is measured on the encoded bag, not on a field's characters — and it is checked BEFORE the object check, so an over-cap OBJECT reports too_long alone.

expect.message: default_attributes must be at most 8192 bytes
op must be put, patch or delete

serverOnly.message: entity_type must be journey or journey_plan_item
serverOnly.why: The client dispatches BY entity_type and so cannot fail this check.

cases.name: journey_plan_item/patch/is-not-an-allowed-op-kind
cases.why: A plan item has no mutable content of its own. Because the description declares journey_id/apiary_id required on put AND patch, both sides validate the payload of the rejected patch identically.

expect.message: op must be put or delete for journey_plan_item (plan items have no patch)

cases.name: todo/patch/completion-only
cases.why: #378: completing a todo uploads status + completed_at, never the title or priority.

cases.name: todo/put/title-whitespace-only-counts-as-absent
cases.why: absentWhen: blank — unlike apiaries' name, validateTodoOp DOES TrimSpace here. Getting the two the same way round is exactly the mistake nothing else catches.

expect.message: title must be at most 500 characters
description must be at most 10000 characters
due_date must be a YYYY-MM-DD date

cases.name: todo/patch/due-date-cleared-to-an-empty-string-is-accepted
cases.why: absentWhen: empty. Describing due_date as null-only would make the client reject every cleared due date.

serverOnly.why: serverOnly (D-20): status is not described at all.

expect.message: completed_at must be an RFC3339 timestamp

cases.name: todo/patch/completed-at-without-a-zone-offset
cases.why: Go's RFC3339Nano demands a Z or ±hh:mm; Dart's DateTime.parse does not. A client leaning on DateTime.parse would accept this and only find out at the next push.

expect.message: completed_at must be an RFC3339 timestamp

serverOnly.why: serverOnly: organization membership is server state.

expect.message: op must be put, patch or delete

serverOnly.why: The client dispatches BY entity_type and so cannot fail this check.
